thread:
dina: heads up, our unit suite started failing after bumping @redwood/inference -> 1.9.0. Local dev (Node 18) blows up with ESM + fetch errors, CI (Node 20) only shows flakiness. Error: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" and later "ReferenceError: fetch is not defined".

ryan: Are tests running under node or jsdom? That matters a lot. If vitest/jest uses jsdom it may polyfill fetch differently.

dina: vitest running with environment: 'node' in our config. We have type: "module" in package.json. We also use ts-node for a few test helpers.

mai: Two axes: module format (ESM) + runtime APIs (fetch/Request). For ESM packages in node_modules, vitest/esbuild may need to transform them. Try adding `deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] }` and `optimizeDeps.include` in vitest config.

alex: For jest it's worse: jest ignores node_modules by default. Use `transformIgnorePatterns` to allow the SDK to be transformed: `transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!(@redwood/inference)/)']`. Also ensure you use `babel-jest` with `modules: false` or `ts-jest` with ESM support.

dina: I tried inline + optimizeDeps but still get `Request is not defined` coming from a typed fetch wrapper in the SDK. It does `new Request(url, opts)` at top-level.

ryan: That means your node test runtime doesn't provide WHATWG Request. Node 18+ has fetch but not always Request in polyfills depending on flags. We usually add `globalThis.fetch = (await import('node-fetch')).default` or `import 'undici/polyfill-fetch'` in setup. In ESM land you need to import the polyfill as ESM.

mai: Another approach: create a small test shim module `tests/shims/fetch-shim.mjs` that does `import { fetch, Request, Headers, Response } from 'undici'` and re-exports them on globalThis. Then point your test runner setup to import that before anything else.

alex: Also check the SDK's package.json "exports" and "type" fields. ESM-only packages sometimes set `"type": "module"` and export subpaths that tools don't understand. For jest you can `moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/inference$': '<rootDir>/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.js' }` to force the exact entry.

dina: Good tip. There's also weirdness where vitest's esbuild leaves top-level await/import.meta untouched if optimizeDeps isn't set. I added `deps.inline` and `transformMode: { web: [/node_modules/] }` and that removed the import syntax issue.

ryan: For mocking, if you need to `vi.mock('@redwood/inference')`, remember that mocking ESM-only packages requires you to use a mock file that is ESM too (.mjs/.ts) and lives in the right place. Vitest will prefer the actual ESM shape; a CJS `__mocks__` won't be picked up.

mai: Concrete vitest example that fixed it for us in a monorepo (ts):
```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'node',
    globals: true,
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] },
    setupFiles: ['./tests/vitest.setup.ts']
  },
  optimizeDeps: { include: ['@redwood/inference'] },
  resolve: { alias: { '@redwood/inference/test-shim': '/tests/mocks/redwood-test-shim.ts' } }
})
```
In `tests/vitest.setup.ts` we `import './shims/fetch-shim.mjs'` then `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', globalThis.fetch)` and `vi.stubGlobal('Request', globalThis.Request)` so the SDK finds them.

dina: Nice. For jest we ended up with a small ESM-compatible mock file `tests/__mocks__/@redwood/inference.mjs` and `jest.config.cjs` has `moduleNameMapper` to point the package name to the mock when `NODE_ENV=test`. Worked around the need for a CJS build.

alex: If anyone else hits `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` when trying to import deep paths, open an issue describing which subpath you tried. In the meantime `moduleNameMapper` or `exportsResolver` in your bundler can route it.

ryan: CI note: our pipeline runs vitest 0.33 + esbuild pinned; local dev was on 0.35 which changed inline transform behavior. Pin versions or align dev images.

mai: Another gotcha: if your tests import mocked modules that themselves import `node:http` or other node builtin shims, vitest's mocking of builtins can cause `Cannot use import statement outside a module` because vi.mock('node:http') creates a virtual module resolved as CJS. For those we create tiny ESM stubs: `tests/mocks/node-http.mjs` and use resolve.alias in vitest to point 'node:http' -> './tests/mocks/node-http.mjs' during tests.

dina: Action items I'm taking: 1) add fetch shim import to vitest setup, 2) inline the package in deps and optimizeDeps, 3) add a test-only alias for node builtins that cause transform issues, 4) pin vitest/esbuild in CI to match local. I'll file a DX issue proposing a test-friendly entrypoint for the SDK (small ESM file that doesn't reference top-level edge APIs).

ci-bot: test-run: CI image currently Node 20, vitest 0.33. Several failures correlated with @redwood/inference 1.9.0. Please include repro steps in issue.

ryan: If you open the issue, include minimal repro (vite/vitest config, package.json type, exact error stacks, node versions). That really speeds up runtime team triage.

mai: Also attach a small patch for consumers: a sample `tests/vitest.setup.ts` and `tests/shims/fetch-shim.mjs` so teams can copy/paste.

dina: Will do. Thanks folks — saved me a day.
